clue.text: Protest against chart presented by Yard showing breakdown of populace

indicators.note: against here means placed right beside, so the next piece follows on

parts.note: a demo is a protest march or rally
a graph is a chart of data

explanation.surface: Campaigners object to a diagram supplied by Scotland Yard about the make-up of the population.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard' suggests Scotland Yard, the London police, but it only gives its abbreviation Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Demography is the statistical study of a population's structure by age, sex, birth rate and so on.

clue.text: What sounds like a note or notes?

indicators.note: sounds like says the spoken form of the next word gives the entry

parts.note: doh is the first note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what word sounds like a musical note, or several of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks musical, but it means banknotes, and dough is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for money, which banknotes are.

clue.text: Town girl has attitude

parts.note: a maid is an old word for a girl
has can be shortened to 's, as in she's got
tone is the attitude a speaker takes

explanation.surface: A small-town young woman is a bit stroppy.
explanation.walkthrough: MAIDSTONE is the county town of Kent, in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidstone is an example of a town, the county town of Kent.

clue.text: Not Johnson's definition of touristic', however impressive?

definitions.text: Not Johnson's definition of touristic', however impressive?

parts.words: Not Johnson's definition of touristic', however impressive
parts.note: Samuel Johnson said of a famous Irish basalt formation that it was worth seeing but not worth going to see, so to him it was no tourist destination however striking

explanation.walkthrough: Dr Samuel Johnson, the dictionary-maker, is the Johnson meant, not Boris: his quip on this County Antrim rock coast is the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated landmark of hexagonal basalt columns in Northern Ireland, which Johnson judged worth seeing but not worth the journey.

clue.text: Beer limiting impression of crunchy food?

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing, so the beer word is wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
a dent is an impression pressed into a surface

explanation.surface: Beer containing an impression of something crunchy to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impression' is a dent, not a feeling; the Italian phrase describes food firm to the bite, hence 'crunchy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for 'to the tooth': pasta or vegetables cooked so they still have some bite.

clue.text: 'Holy 'can get

annotationWithheld.why: Held as "'Holy 'can get" (7): HOLY CAN is anagram fodder for HALCYON, but the clue is cut short and has no definition; no reprint or search gives the missing words.

clue.text: Sticks around, being self satisfied

indicators.note: around says the word for sticks is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: gums means sticks, as with glue

explanation.surface: Someone who glues things together and is pleased with themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns GUMS back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug describes someone excessively pleased with their own achievements.

clue.text: Sound scientist wanting nothing of sexual assertiveness?

parts.note: Ernst Mach studied sound and shock waves, and the Mach number measuring speed against sound is named after him
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: An acoustics researcher with no interest in aggressive sexuality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' looks like a deletion, but here the scientist wants (needs) nothing, so O is added after MACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho describes an aggressively masculine, sexually assertive manner.

clue.text: Faldo's game, sinking dead short distance-a birdie

indicators.note: sinking means taking something down into itself, so the game word swallows the next piece

parts.note: Nick Faldo is an English golfer, so his game is golf
an inch is a short distance

explanation.surface: Faldo on the golf course, holing a putt from just inches away for a birdie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinking' puts D inside GOLF. 'Birdie' is a golf score in the surface, but here it means a small bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The goldfinch is a small brightly coloured songbird, a little bird.

clue.text: Short respite for taking on oxygen before interplanetary area?

indicators.note: before places the breathing piece ahead of the next one

parts.note: breathing is taking air, and its oxygen, into the lungs
space is the region between the planets

explanation.surface: An astronaut pauses to take on air before heading out into the void.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pause or rest from effort, time to recover.

clue.text: University almost late providing gear for work-out

indicators.note: almost means the word for late loses its final letter

parts.note: tardy means late

explanation.surface: A student running behind provides kit for a gym session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of TARDY.
explanation.definitionFit: A unitard is a one-piece close-fitting garment worn for exercise or dance.

clue.text: Songlike, delicate line recalled around middle of aria

indicators.note: around says the reversed pieces wrap the central letters
recalled means called back, so the two pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: lacy means delicate, like lace

indicators.note: middle of takes the inner letters of the word aria

explanation.surface: A singer's delicate phrase is brought back to the heart of an aria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses both pieces together, giving LYCAL, and 'around' wraps that round the inner letters of 'aria'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrical means expressive and song-like, like the words of a song.

clue.text: Athens — icy 'when broadcast leads to some doubt

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of the two words are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A frosty reception in Athens, once it goes on air, makes people uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when broadcast' rearranges ATHENS and ICY.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitancy is a state of indecision or uncertainty, a measure of doubt.

clue.text: A return to dope makes you detached

indicators.note: return means the word for dope comes back the other way

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an idiot

explanation.surface: Going back to drugs leaves you cut off from others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' suggests drugs, but it is a fool, which 'return' reverses to LOOF.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof means distant and uninvolved, standing apart from others.

clue.text: One in bed's laid back, not 2 mentioning the pain

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other
laid back means the beds word is set the opposite way round

parts.note: cots are beds
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A relaxed patient in hospital who keeps quiet about the pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid back' turns COTS into STOC, and I goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoical person endures suffering without complaint, never voicing it.

clue.text: Glass sure becomes molten, lacking certain grains?

indicators.note: molten glass flows into new shapes, so these letters are melted and reformed

explanation.surface: Glass melts down, surely, as its sand grains fuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes molten' rearranges GLASS and SURE. The grains are of sugar, not the sand glass is made from.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugarless means containing no sugar, a sweetener sold in grains.

clue.text: A German had seaside town given name of Dutch city

parts.note: ein is German for a
had can be shortened to 'd, as in I'd
Hove is a seaside town beside Brighton on the south coast of England

explanation.surface: A German tourist visited an English resort, then named a city in the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Eindhoven is a large city in the south of the Netherlands, home of Philips.

clue.text: It's Victor (curious artist)

indicators.note: curious means odd or strange, so the letters are put into a strange new order

explanation.surface: An odd painter called Victor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curious' rearranges IT'S and VICTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A Vorticist was a member of a British avant-garde art movement around 1914.

clue.text: Energy -more energy then part fails

parts.note: go means energy or vigour
E is the abbreviation for energy
sunder means to part or split

explanation.surface: A machine with ever more power until a component breaks down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' looks like a noun, a component, but it is the verb meaning to split.
explanation.definitionFit: To go under is to fail, as a business does when it collapses.

clue.text: Sea rising? Get ready to leave bar

parts.note: the drink is slang for the sea
up means rising, going higher

explanation.surface: A flood tide warning sends drinkers out of the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' is informal for the sea; 'Drink up' is what a barman calls at closing time.
explanation.definitionFit: Finishing your glass is what customers are told to do at closing time.

clue.text: A set of races in mostly grand surroundings- Henley?

indicators.note: in says the A and races go inside the shortened grand word
mostly means the word for grand loses its last letter

parts.note: regal means grand, stately
the TT is the Tourist Trophy series of motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A series of contests held in stately surroundings, perhaps at Henley.
explanation.walkthrough: Henley-on-Thames, a town west of London, holds a famous annual rowing event, which the question mark marks as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Henley is an example of a series of boat races, the annual Henley Royal event.

clue.text: No cheer for girl

parts.note: rah is a cheer, as in hurrah

explanation.surface: Nobody applauds the young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Norah is a girl's name.

clue.text: Show always bringing in University backing

indicators.note: bringing in means taking something inside, so one piece contains the other
backing means going backwards, so the word for always is reversed

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: A production that the university always supports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns EVER into REVE, and U goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a theatrical entertainment of sketches, songs and dances.

clue.text: Composer contributing to cover disc

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A composer writes music for a recording of cover versions.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was an Italian opera writer, of Aida and La Traviata.

clue.text: Taking in ridiculous egoist in pub

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters go inside the pub word

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: ridiculous means absurd, so the letters are put into an absurd order

explanation.surface: Accepting a preposterous self-obsessed person in the local bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' looks like a link word or verb, but it is the definition, as the noun phrase 'taking in' is not a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingestion is the act of taking food or drink into the body.

clue.text: Poverty-stricken-born and died before end of day

indicators.note: before puts the born and died pieces ahead of the last one

parts.note: née means born, used before a woman's maiden name

indicators.note: end of takes the final letter of the word day

explanation.surface: A pauper's life, from birth to death within a single day.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy means lacking money and the necessities of life, poor.

clue.text: Take note of weapon, one carried by aircraftsman

indicators.note: carried by means held inside, so the aircraftsman word holds the others

parts.note: erk is British RAF slang for an aircraftsman, a low-ranking airman
an arm is a weapon
a means one

explanation.surface: Note the gun a junior airman is carrying.
explanation.walkthrough: An erk is British forces slang for the lowest-ranking airman; 'carried by' puts the weapon and A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark something is to set it aside or mark it for special attention.

clue.text: Side keeping it back before end of game (late afternoon)

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the side word holds the next piece

parts.note: a side is a team

indicators.note: back means the word it is turned the other way
end of takes the last letter of the word game

explanation.surface: A team holding on before the final whistle, late in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns 'it' round, which 'keeping' places inside the side; the bracketed '(late afternoon)' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Teatime is the time of day for afternoon tea, around four or five o'clock.

clue.text: Aquarius, perhaps, mostly carrying weak drink

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the shortened sign holds the next piece
mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: Aquarius is an example of a star sign

explanation.surface: A water-carrier holding a feeble drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts SIGN to SIG, which 'carrying' wraps round W. Aquarius is the water-carrier of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: A swig is a large gulp of drink.

clue.text: A strand involving father, it seems

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so the strand word holds the father word

parts.note: ply is a strand of rope or yarn
a father is a parent

explanation.surface: A thread wound round a dad, so it appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'father' gives the general word for either parent rather than a title such as PA.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparently means seemingly, as far as one can tell.
